Structural connectivity (schaefer400_tian_structural_connectivity, destrieux_tian_structural_connectivity): the mean over 100 HCP Young Adult subjects of the number of streamlines joining two regions of the Schaefer 400 and Tian S2 atlases, and of the Destrieux parcels and Tian's, computed by NeuroLang (tools/hcp_connectivity/tractography.py; the dataset: https://gitlab.inria.fr/dwasserm/neurolang-hcp-connectivity) as follows. For each subject, from the HCP's minimally preprocessed diffusion MRI in its T1w space: response functions (dwi2response dhollander) and multi-shell multi-tissue constrained spherical deconvolution (dwi2fod msmt_csd); the five-tissue-type image of its FreeSurfer segmentation (5ttgen freesurfer); 5 million streamlines of anatomically constrained probabilistic tractography (tckgen iFOD2, ACT, backtracking, cropped at the grey/white matter interface, dynamic seeding); SIFT2 weights (tcksift2); Schaefer's and Tian's atlases brought from MNI space to the subject through the HCP's warp (nearest neighbour), and Destrieux's parcels of the subject's own FreeSurfer segmentation (aparc.a2009s); the streamlines whose two ends lie within 2 mm of two regions counted (tck2connectome -symmetric -zero_diagonal -assignment_radial_search 2). The counts are then averaged over the subjects. With MRtrix3: Tournier J-D, Smith R, Raffelt D, et al. MRtrix3: a fast, flexible and open software framework for medical image processing and visualisation. NeuroImage 202:116137 (2019). doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2019.116137; anatomically constrained: Smith RE, Tournier J-D, Calamante F, Connelly A. NeuroImage 62:1924-1938 (2012). doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2012.06.005; SIFT2: Smith RE, Tournier J-D, Calamante F, Connelly A. NeuroImage 119:338-351 (2015). doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2015.06.092. The atlases: Schaefer A, Kong R, Gordon EM, et al. Cerebral Cortex 28:3095-3114 (2018). doi:10.1093/cercor/bhx179; Destrieux C, Fischl B, Dale A, Halgren E. NeuroImage 53:1-15 (2010). doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2010.06.010; Tian Y, Margulies DS, Breakspear M, Zalesky A. Nature Neuroscience 23:1421-1432 (2020). doi:10.1038/s41593-020-00711-6. The Human Connectome Project: Van Essen DC, Smith SM, Barch DM, Behrens TEJ, Yacoub E, Ugurbil K. NeuroImage 80:62-79 (2013). doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2013.05.041. Data were provided [in part] by the Human Connectome Project, WU-Minn Consortium (Principal Investigators: David Van Essen and Kamil Ugurbil; 1U54MH091657) funded by the 16 NIH Institutes and Centers that support the NIH Blueprint for Neuroscience Research; and by the McDonnell Center for Systems Neuroscience at Washington University.

Resting-state functional connectivity (schaefer400_tian_functional_connectivity, destrieux_tian_functional_connectivity): the HCP Young Adult resting-state fMRI of 964 subjects, computed by NeuroLang (tools/hcp_connectivity/functional.py; the dataset: https://gitlab.inria.fr/dwasserm/neurolang-hcp-connectivity) as follows. For each subject, each of its four runs of rest (rfMRI_REST1/2, LR and RL; ICA-FIX cleaned, MSMAll aligned, 91,282 grayordinates, no global signal regression): the time series averaged within each region (the cortical parcels of the atlas, Tian's subcortical regions); the Pearson correlation of each pair of regions (a full correlation, not a partial one); its Fisher z, averaged over the four runs. The z are then averaged over the subjects and turned back into a correlation (tanh). Smith SM et al. Resting-state fMRI in the Human Connectome Project. NeuroImage 80:144-168 (2013). doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2013.05.039. Glasser MF et al. The minimal preprocessing pipelines for the Human Connectome Project. NeuroImage 80:105-124 (2013). doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2013.04.127. Salimi-Khorshidi G et al. Automatic denoising of functional MRI data: combining independent component analysis and hierarchical fusion of classifiers. NeuroImage 90:449-468 (2014). doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2013.11.046. Robinson EC et al. Multimodal surface matching with higher-order smoothness constraints. NeuroImage 167:453-465 (2018). doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2017.10.037. Data were provided [in part] by the Human Connectome Project, WU-Minn Consortium (Principal Investigators: David Van Essen and Kamil Ugurbil; 1U54MH091657) funded by the 16 NIH Institutes and Centers that support the NIH Blueprint for Neuroscience Research; and by the McDonnell Center for Systems Neuroscience at Washington University.
